- Primary use case: customer support triage + localized FAQ generation (strict factual accuracy).
- Constraint: EU data residency and audit logs are required for PII-bearing traffic.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a small sample (1k rows) of anonymized CS transcripts per locale (link looks fine).
2) We run a 2-week evaluation across 3 model families with locale-specific prompt sets.
3) Deliverables: per-locale accuracy/QA metrics, hallucination analysis, latency/cost estimates, recommended model variant.

Attached: prompt_set_v1.csv (starter prompts for DE/FR/JP).

Can you confirm the sample share + priority locales? We’ll schedule an internal SE pairing (cc’d) to scope the eval.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & multilingual evals (DE/FR/JP) - recommended models & eval plan

Hi Sophie — quick technical follow-up and our recommended shortlist for the eval.

Recommendation (initial run):
- Family A: Open LLM (instruction-tuned) - e.g., Mistral/Falcon variants (fast, low cost)
- Family B: LLaMA-derived medium (quantized int8/4) - better on EU languages in our prior tests
- Family C: Larger instruction-tuned model (higher cost) for a control baseline (safety/QA).

Evaluation plan (2 weeks):
- Per-locale prompt set (attached) + fuzz tests.
- Metrics: exact-match for FAQ answers, hallucination rate (fact checks), token-level latency, cost per 1k requests.
- Regression checks: include English baseline prompts to detect cross-locale regressions after tuning.

Links/benchmarks: 
- Prior locale eval snapshot: https://dashboard.redwood.com/benchmarks/globex-4521
- Internal LOE / perf notes: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/globex-sample-data

Attachments: locale_eval_results_q1.pdf (samples from previous internal runs illustrating DE gap).

Notes on mitigations for German hallucinations: 
- Use stricter provenance prompts (source recall), reduce creative decoding temperature, and add a post-check classifier for hallucination detection.
- If customers require, can test small supervised fine-tune vs instruction-tuning; the latter tends to be cheaper but less effective on strict factuality.

I’ll provision the eval cluster in EU region (Redwood Dedicated/private options) once we get confirmation on sample & SLA constraints.

—Nikhil

nikhil@redwood.com

Thanks Nikhil — helpful. A few clarifying Qs: 
1) Hallucination classifier: is that run as a separate service or inline with inference? Impact on latency?
2) Fine-tuning vs instruction-tuning: If we need high factuality for DE, are you seeing consistent wins from supervised fine-tune? What’s the cost/time delta?
3) Data residency: we must ensure data never leaves EU for the eval. Can Redwood guarantee this for the eval duration?

Also, are there any redlines we should expect in the SLA for regulatory audits? Lars — feel free to add.

Best,
Sophie
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@globexretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T14:15:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & multilingual evals (DE/FR/JP) - answers + SLA draft

Hi Sophie — quick answers inline: 

1) Hallucination classifier: can be inline as a lightweight post-filter (adds ~30–60ms P95 depending on model). We can also run a batched async verifier if latency budget is strict.

2) Fine-tune vs instruction-tune: supervised fine-tune shows stronger gains on strict QA tasks in German; timeline ~2–3 weeks for a small supervised run + validation. Approx cost multiple: ~2–3x compared to instruction-tuning evaluation (depends on dataset size).

3) Data residency: we can run the eval entirely in EU region (Redwood Dedicated / Private). We will not move raw samples outside the EU and will provide audit logs; we also support KMS-backed keying for any persisted artifacts.

Attached: sla_draft.docx (initial draft), and a DocuSign link for a short eval MSA in case legal wants to expedite.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm sample share (done) and sign the short eval MSA (optional).
- We start the EU eval cluster next Tuesday and deliver initial results in ~10 business days.

If that timeline works I’ll book the SE time and provision EU capacity.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
